sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 Phonology = 2.1 inventory, 2.2 diphthongs, 2.3 syllable structure, 2.4 contrasts, 2.5 distribution, 2.6 clusters/gemination; no suprasegmental subsection (the volume's '2.8.4 Stress' passage belongs to the Toda chapter). Ch. 2 sec. 2.1 'Soliga bhasha dhvaniracane' (pp. 55-62) lists Soliga-vs-standard-Kannada sound correspondences plus vowel and consonant charts; no term for stress (ottu / balaghata / svarabhara / aghata) occurs (Kannada scanned of the section, a full-text search for stress/accent + read).

sources.citation: Si, Aung. 2012. The traditional ecological knowledge of the Solega: a linguistic perspective. PhD thesis, Australian National University (xiv+366 leaves; Appendix A 'A Sketch Grammar of Solega', Appendix B lexicon). hdl 1885/149874, doi 10.25911/5d5e75b032ef7.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix A sec. 1 'Solega Phonology' has only 1.1 phoneme inventory (consonants, vowels incl. length and nasalisation contrasts), 1.2 general comments (orthography), 1.3 processes at morpheme boundaries, 1.4 syllable structure; no stress/accent/prosody statement anywhere in the sketch (a full-text search for stress/accent whole text for stress/accent/prosod/suprasegmental + reading of 1.1.2-1.4). Variety: Five-clan (aidu kula) Solega of the B.R. Hills, Karnataka.
